full_description: About Us Circle is building the world’s leading AI-powered, all-in-one platform for digital businesses. This team focuses on building the infrastructure to measure, diagnose, and improve production AI systems, rather than ML research or model training. We're looking for a Lead Engineer to help us build out the evaluation frameworks, observability tooling, and diagnostic infrastructure that tell us whether our AI Agents are working well, where to improve them, and how to make them faster and more cost-efficient. Lead and grow the AI Quality engineering team. Set technical direction and manage day-to-day priorities, all while staying hands-on in the code yourself. Partner closely with AI Core engineering. Ruby on Rails is our production system and the foundation that Circle’s AI Agents are built on and proficiency in Python is a strong plus, especially for the data and evaluation side of the work. Experience building evaluation or observability infrastructure for ML/AI systems. Experience designing datasets, annotation workflows, or labeling pipelines for ML/AI evaluation. You know how to turn raw examples into a dataset you can trust through human annotation, AI-generated data, or simulation. Learn fast, experiment aggressively, and thrive in a highly dynamic environment. You’ll need to be comfortable running a lot of experiments and letting the results settle the argument, including the ones that don't work (which will be many of them in the beginning). Investigate quality issues and support remediation with the groups that produce and consume the data. Design failover, outage, and volume tests and judge the evidence, including recovery time and recovery point. The platform team executes destructive and chaos tests. Run read-only checks in pre-production and production. Integrate quality checks with CI/CD on GitHub Actions or an equivalent tool. Use AWS and Grafana to observe pipeline health, including CloudWatch metrics, secrets metadata, and container platform state. Check classification, masking, and retention against the stated data rules. Track defects to closure in Jira and keep test cases and results in TestRail. Provide quality evidence, risks, and readiness input for releases. Use an AI coding assistant to analyze data and author SQL, Python, and quality checks, and review generated output before it is used. Strong SQL and Snowflake data-modelling experience, including layered raw, history, silver, and gold models, reconciliation and drift queries, and slowly changing dimensions and merge behavior. Experience with logical and physical data models and with assessing the downstream impact of schema and data-contract changes. Experience validating PostgreSQL sources, including consistent snapshot counts and logical replication. Hands-on Python automation for data comparison and reconciliation, using pytest or an equivalent framework. Experience running and reading orchestrated pipelines in Airflow or an equivalent scheduler. Experience validating data movement, transformation, completeness, history, freshness, and compliance from source systems into analytical datasets. Experience diagnosing data quality issues and supporting remediation. Experience integrating data quality checks with CI/CD using GitHub Actions or equivalent tools. Experience with test management and defect tracking in TestRail and Jira. Working knowledge of AWS and Grafana for pipeline observation, including CloudWatch, secrets management, and container platforms. Experience designing resilience tests and judging evidence for failover, outage, volume, and recovery objectives. Working knowledge of data classification, masking, and retention checks. Experience producing data quality metrics, reports, and dashboards. Experience with risk-based testing in Agile or Kanban teams. Hands-on use of AI coding assistants (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, or equivalent) to author SQL, Python, and quality checks, with human review of generated output. Ability to communicate clearly with engineering and business stakeholders. Experience providing quality evidence, risks, and readiness input for releases. Nice to have: Experience observing Snowflake Openflow or NiFi connector state well enough to recognize a stalled load. Experience with custom cross-table data quality checks that publish results for dashboarding. Familiarity with GenAI, LLMs, and agentic workflows for maintaining data quality checks. Familiarity with RAG and MCP concepts for QE tooling and for generating test data. Knowledge of AI-driven test optimization and coverage analytics (SeaLights or equivalent). Experience with service virtualization using WireMock or an equivalent tool, so checks can run when a dependency is unavailable. Experience specifying and reviewing dbt tests. full_description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover
